description: Pozole Rojo is a beloved traditional Mexican soup, rich with tender pork and hearty hominy, all swimming in a vibrant, savory red chile broth. This comforting and flavorful dish is a staple for celebrations and family gatherings, offering a taste of Mexico in every spoonful. Its complex flavors come from a blend of dried chiles, garlic, and spices, making it truly unforgettable.

ingredients.notes: stemmed and seeded, optional for extra heat and color

instructions.title: Prepare the Pork
instructions.text: In a large pot, combine the pork shoulder cubes, half of the onion, 4 unpeeled garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, and 1 tablespoon of salt. Cover with approximately 10 cups of water or chicken broth. Bring to a rolling boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface during cooking.

instructions.title: Rehydrate the Chiles
instructions.text: While the pork is cooking, lightly toast the dried guajillo, ancho, and cascabel chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side until they become fragrant. Be careful not to burn them, as this can make them bitter. Transfer the toasted chiles to a heatproof bowl, cover them with hot water, and let them soak for 20-30 minutes until they are fully softened.

instructions.title: Make the Chile Puree
instructions.text: Once the chiles are softened, drain them and discard the soaking water. In a blender, combine the drained chiles, the remaining quarter of the onion, 2 peeled garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon of dried Mexican oregano, 0.5 teaspoon of ground cumin, and about 1.5 cups of the pork cooking broth. Blend until the mixture is very smooth. Strain the chile puree through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing firmly on the solids to extract all the flavorful liquid. Discard any remaining solids.

instructions.title: Combine Pork, Hominy, and Broth
instructions.text: Carefully remove the cooked pork from the pot and shred it or cut it into smaller, bite-sized pieces. Discard the cooked onion, garlic, and bay leaves from the broth. Return the shredded pork to the pot with the remaining broth. Add the drained and rinsed canned hominy and the strained red chile puree to the pot. Stir everything together gently.

instructions.title: Simmer and Season
instructions.text: Bring the pozole to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Stir well to ensure all ingredients are thoroughly combined. Taste the broth and adjust the seasoning with additional salt as needed. Allow the pozole to simmer for at least 30 minutes, or up to an hour, uncovered, to allow the flavors to fully meld and deepen. The longer it simmers, the richer the taste.

instructions.title: Serve with Garnishes
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Pozole Rojo into individual serving bowls. Serve immediately with a generous array of traditional garnishes on the side, such as finely shredded cabbage, thinly sliced radishes, diced white onion, fresh lime wedges, and a sprinkle of dried Mexican oregano. Offer warm tostadas or crusty bread for dipping.

tips: For a deeper, richer flavor, lightly toast your dried chiles in a dry skillet for a minute or two before rehydrating them. This brings out their natural oils and aromatic qualities.
If you prefer a thicker broth, you can remove a cup of hominy from the pot, mash it, and then return it to the soup. This adds a nice body without altering the flavor.
Pozole Rojo tastes even better the next day as the flavors continue to develop. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days and reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Pozole Rojo, a culinary masterpiece from the heart of Mexico, is more than just a soup; it's a celebration in a bowl. Rich, hearty, and deeply satisfying, this traditional Mexican stew has graced tables for centuries, particularly during festive occasions and family gatherings. Imagine tender pieces of pork, plump kernels of hominy, all swimming in a vibrant, savory broth infused with the earthy warmth of dried red chiles. It’s a dish that speaks to the soul, comforting and invigorating with every spoonful. If you're ready to embark on a flavorful journey and bring the authentic taste of Mexico into your kitchen, this comprehensive guide to crafting the perfect Pozole Rojo is for you.

## What is Pozole Rojo?

At its core, Pozole Rojo is a traditional Mexican soup or stew made with hominy (large, dried corn kernels that have been nixtamalized), meat (most commonly pork, but sometimes chicken), and a rich, red chile broth. The term "Rojo" refers specifically to this characteristic red color, which comes from a blend of dried red chiles like guajillos and anchos, often with a touch of arbol chiles for heat.

The history of pozole dates back to pre-Hispanic times, with corn being a sacred staple in Mesoamerican cultures. Over centuries, it evolved, incorporating pork after the Spanish conquest, becoming the beloved dish we know today. What makes Pozole Rojo so special is the depth of flavor achieved through slow cooking. The pork is simmered until incredibly tender, while the chiles are rehydrated and blended into a robust, aromatic sauce that forms the soul of the broth. It's a dish often served for special occasions such as Mexican Independence Day, Christmas, New Year's Eve, or any significant family reunion, embodying warmth, tradition, and togetherness.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating an authentic Pozole Rojo requires a few key components. Here's what you'll need for a recipe that typically serves 6-8 people:

For the Pork:
* 2-3 lbs pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 2-inch chunks
* 1 large white onion, quartered
* 6-8 cloves garlic, peeled and smashed
* 2-3 bay leaves
* 2 tablespoons salt, plus more to taste
* 12-14 cups water or low-sodium chicken/pork broth

For the Red Chile Sauce:
* 10-12 dried guajillo chiles, stems and seeds removed
* 3-4 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
* 2-3 dried arbol chiles (optional, for heat), stems and seeds removed
* 4-5 cloves garlic, peeled
* 1/2 small white onion
* 1 teaspoon dried Mexican oregano
* 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
* 1/2 cup reserved cooking liquid from pork or water

For the Soup Assembly:
* 2 (25 oz) cans large white hominy, drained and rinsed
* Remaining reserved pork cooking liquid

For Serving & Garnish (Crucial!):
* Shredded green cabbage or lettuce
* Thinly sliced radishes
* Diced white onion
* Fresh cilantro, chopped
* Lime wedges
* Tostadas or warm corn tortillas
* Sliced avocado (optional)
* Crema Mexicana or sour cream (optional)

## Step-by-Step Pozole Rojo Recipe

Follow these steps to create a truly unforgettable Pozole Rojo:

Step 1: Cook the Pork
Place the pork chunks in a large stockpot or Dutch oven. Add the quartered onion, smashed garlic cloves, bay leaves, and 2 tablespoons of salt. Pour in enough water or broth to cover the pork by at least 2 inches (about 12-14 cups). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 to 3 hours, or until the pork is fall-apart tender. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface during the first hour of cooking. Once cooked, remove the pork from the pot and set aside to cool slightly. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding the solids, and reserve the broth. Shred the cooled pork using two forks.

Step 2: Prepare the Red Chile Sauce
While the pork cooks, prepare the chile sauce. Lightly toast the dried guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side, being careful not to burn them. Transfer the toasted chiles to a heatproof bowl and cover them with hot water. Let them soak for 20-30 minutes, or until softened. Drain the chiles, reserving about 1/2 cup of the soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, fresh garlic cloves, 1/2 small onion, Mexican oregano, cumin, and the reserved soaking liquid. Blend until very smooth. For a silky broth, press the chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, using a spoon or spatula to push through as much pulp as possible and discarding any remaining solids.

Step 3: Assemble the Pozole
In your large, clean stockpot, combine the strained red chile sauce, the shredded pork, and the drained and rinsed hominy. Pour in 8-10 cups of the reserved pork cooking liquid (or more, depending on your desired consistency). Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook, uncovered, for at least 30-45 minutes, allowing all the flavors to meld beautifully. Taste and adjust salt as needed. The longer it simmers, the deeper the flavor will be.

## Expert Tips for Perfect Pozole Rojo

* Quality Chiles Matter: Use fresh, pliable dried chiles. If they are brittle or dusty, they might be old. Toasting them briefly in a dry pan before soaking deepens their flavor.
* Don't Skip Straining: Straining the chile sauce is crucial for that smooth, restaurant-quality broth. It removes any tough skin or seeds, resulting in a more refined texture.
* Tender Pork is Key: Cook the pork until it easily shreds. This ensures a melt-in-your-mouth experience in every bite of your Pozole Rojo.
* Hominy Options: While canned hominy is convenient, dried hominy, which requires soaking overnight and cooking until tender, offers a superior, chewier texture if you have the time.
* Let it Rest: Like many stews, Pozole Rojo often tastes even better the next day. The flavors continue to develop and deepen, making leftovers a real treat.
* Adjust Heat to Your Liking: The arbol chiles provide most of the heat. Adjust the quantity, or omit them entirely, to suit your spice preference.

## Serving & Garnish Ideas

Serving Pozole Rojo is an art form in itself, as the garnishes are just as important as the soup. Set out a "pozole bar" for guests to customize their bowls:

* Freshly shredded green cabbage or crisp lettuce provides a refreshing crunch.
* Thinly sliced radishes offer a peppery bite and beautiful color.
* Diced white onion and chopped fresh cilantro are essential aromatics.
* Lots of lime wedges are a must for squeezing over the soup, brightening all the flavors.
* Serve with warm, crispy tostadas or soft corn tortillas for dipping.
* For added richness, offer slices of creamy avocado or a dollop of crema Mexicana (Mexican sour cream).
* A few dashes of your favorite hot sauce can also add an extra kick.

## Pozole Rojo Variations & Substitutions

While this recipe focuses on the classic pork Pozole Rojo, there are delightful variations:

* Chicken Pozole (Pozole de Pollo): Substitute pork with bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks work well). Cook similarly until tender, then shred.
* Vegetarian Pozole: Replace meat with hearty mushrooms (like cremini or shiitake), squash, or even plant-based protein. Use vegetable broth instead of pork broth.
* Other Chile Blends: Experiment with adding a few dried pasilla chiles for a deeper, earthier flavor profile, or a smoky chipotle for extra kick.
* Pozole Verde: A vibrant green version made with tomatillos, jalapeños, poblanos, and cilantro.
* Pozole Blanco: This version has a clear broth, without the addition of chiles, relying entirely on the garnishes to provide flavor and color.

Pozole Rojo is a testament to the rich culinary heritage of Mexico – a dish that’s both comforting and celebratory. By following this recipe, you’re not just making a meal; you’re creating an experience. So gather your ingredients, take your time, and savor the process of bringing this incredible Mexican classic to life in your own kitchen. Enjoy every heartwarming spoonful of your homemade Pozole Rojo!
